- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10%.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends; adjust downward bias by adding 2–5% of the recent 7-day average to forecast.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after a price spike; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 10–15% of the spike magnitude from the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted; if price drops below 70% of recent 30-day average, add 2–5% to forecast to encourage recovery.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are too optimistic in early periods; apply a 3–5% downward bias for days 1–7, then adjust linearly toward true trend.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 5 days are above 80% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–8% to prevent over-optimism.
